key_insight: Distal weight-bearing implants require coordinated geometry, biomaterial interfaces, and loading design to support durable bone–implant fixation.
engineering_relevance: Graded Ti–hydroxyapatite interfaces offer mechanistic promise, but implant design must also address gait-induced stresses, micromotion, fatigue, and coating integrity.
method: Systematic review of implant geometry, biomaterials, and clinical translation
Synthesis of gait-phase finite element modeling and osseointegration evidence
Quantitative trend analysis of 34 direct-contribution papers and 32 empirical studies
evidence_signal: More than half of the empirical evidence remained at bench or simulation level, with animal and human studies providing a smaller validation layer.
watch_item: Evidence for graded Ti–hydroxyapatite architectures came predominantly from non-DWBI analog studies, not DWBI-specific validation.
paper_title: Biomaterials and biomechanical design of distal weight-bearing implants: Computational modeling, biomaterial interfaces, and clinical translation
